1  2 FA 1346-2019-J.odt CORAM : NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.
DATE OF RESERVING THE JUDGMENT : 10/03/2026 DATE OF PRONOUNCING THE JUDGMENT: 30/03/2026 JUDGMENT

This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'M.V. Act') by the Appellant - Insurance Company against the judgment and award dated 20/07/2018 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhandara (for short, 'Tribunal') in MACP No. 51/2013,
allowing the Claim Petition against the Appellant and Respondent no. 5 (Original Respondent no. 1),
and awarding the compensation of Rs. 57,67,054/- with interest @ 6% per annum.

2. The above referred Claim Petition was preferred by the Respondent nos. 1 and 4 against the Respondent no. 5 and the Appellant for compensation with the contention that, on 05/12/2012 at about 08.00 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding from the National Highway No. 6 on his motorcycle, the Trailer bearing no. MG-31/AP-4779, which was coming from the backside in a rash and negligent manner, gave dash to the motorcycle of the deceased and the accident took place.
The 3 FA 1346-2019-J.odt deceased succumbed to the injuries.
The necessary evidence was led by the Claimants.
The relevant documents were brought on record.
The Respondent no. 5 examined himself.
The witness was examined from the office of Regional Transport, Bhandara to show that, he was holding a valid driving licence.
On appreciating the evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and award.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the Appellant- Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the Claimants.
Perused the papers.

(a) It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Appellant-Insurance Company that,
the negligence on the part of the Trailer/Truck/Tanker was not proved by the Claimants.
No eye witness was examined by the Claimants.
The factum of involvement of the insured vehicle was not proved.
The Appeal be allowed.

(b) It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Claimants that, the police papers brought on record shows that, the offence was registered against Respondent no. 5,
who was the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent no. 5 4 FA 1346-2019-J.odt who examined himself as a witness, was interested witness.
The learned Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record and the Appeal be dismissed.

4. The pleadings and papers on record shows that, the death of Lalchand Rahule due to road traffic accident on 05/12/2012 while he was driving the motorcycle on National High Way No.6, is not in Shriram General Insurance Co. sentences.text: The challenge to the impugned award is on the point of negligence.
Undisputedly, the Claimants are not the eye witness to the accident.
They placed reliance on the police papers.
Undisputedly, the Crime was registered against the unknown vehicle and driver.

However, the Form 'AA' at Exh. 31 shows that, the Truck bearing no. MH-31/AP-4779 as the offending vehicle, which was registered in the name of Respondent no. 5 and insured with the Appellant - Insurance Company at the relevant time.
The Respondent no. 5 examined himself by filing evidence affidavit below Exh. 56.
He deposed that, on 05/12/2012, he was driving the Truck/Tanker from Nagpur towards Raipur and the deceased was driving the motorcycle towards Zilla Parishad Square.
The deceased himself fell down on the road.
He did not dash the deceased's 5 FA 1346-2019-J.odt motorcycle.
This shows that, his presence on the road and at the place where the accident took place, was admitted.
From the evidence of Respondent no. 5, it is clear that, the accident was not a head-on collision.
He was cross-examined on behalf of the Claimants.
It has come in his cross-examination that, he did not know whether the deceased was riding his motorcycle from the left side of the road and in a moderate speed.
This evidence by Respondent no. 5 in cross-examination shows that, he did not disclose the true story or facts.
When he was the eye witness to the incident/accident, he is bound to know the full factual aspects.
This evidence indicate that, he cannot be fully relied.
The spot panchanama show that, the spot of accident was on the tar road.

5. The learned Tribunal while answering the issue in respect of rash and negligent driving of the vehicle, made the following observations:-
"11.
It is seen that D.W.1 testified that on the date of accident, he was on the spot of accident on N. H. No.6 and driving his aforesaid vehicle.
He further deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself, the accident took place and his vehicle was no way involved in the said accident.
Then, the question crops up as 6 FA 1346-2019-J.odt to why he had not reported the matter to police when the accident took place in his presence.
Even otherwise, he did not take any efforts to provide immediate medical aid to the deceased.
From his conduct, an adverse inference needs to be drawn against him that the accident took place due to dash given by his vehicle and thereafter he ran away from the spot.

No doubt respondent No.2 had filed on record, certified copies of depositions of informant and pach witness,
in criminal case No.371/2013.
However, the claimants did not get an opportunity to cross-examine them.
Therefore, evidence recorded in the aforesaid criminal case is not binding on the claimants.
Thus, that evidence directly cannot be read in this case.
12. There is substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the claimants that the findings given by the criminal court in criminal case are not binding on this Tribunal.
In view of evidence brought on record, there remains no doubt that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the aforesaid trailer by respondent no.1.
In view of above discussion, I accept the submission of the learned advocate for the claimants and there is no force in the submission of the learned advocate for respondent No.2.
Therefore, I am not inclined to accept his submission.

Hence,
I answer point No.1 in the affirmative."

sentences.text: The above referred observations by the learned Trial Court are based on the evidence available on record.

Undisputedly, the Respondent no. 5 was holding the licence to drive the Transport vehicle and this again fortifies his evidence 7 FA 1346-2019-J.odt that, he was driving the Truck/Trailer at the time of accident.
It is needless to state that, no strict proof of evidence is required while dealing with the Claim Petitions under the M.V. Act.
The view taken by the learned Tribunal, therefore, do not call for any interference.
Hence, the following order:-
ORDER i) The Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
ii) The amount deposited by the Appellant - Insurance Company under the award is permitted to be withdrawn by the Claimants, if not withdrawn earlier, with interest accrued thereon.
iii) The balance amount under the award, if any, to be deposited by the Appellant - Insurance Company, within a period of six (6) weeks.
iv) R & P be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
[NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.] B.T.K. Signed by: Mr. B.T. Khapekar Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 30/03/2026 20:39:17
